title: Why Diogenes Told an Emperor to Move
northStar: Wealth and power cannot bribe someone whose peace is not for sale.
sources: Plutarch, Life of Alexander 14 (reported confrontation at Corinth)
Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers VI.38 (Diogenes of Sinope)

lines.text: The world's richest conqueror offered him literally anything.
Diogenes lived inside a giant clay jar in Corinth with zero money, zero status.
Ancient writers record Alexander the Great standing right over him.
He asked softly, name any favor I can grant you right now.
Diogenes didn't even blink. [pause] Yes, stand a little out of my sunlight.
Power cannot bribe someone who already owns his peaceful morning, which is why
